intro_paragraph: Carats is a full-stack JavaScript framework that provides a modern development experience without relying on React. It uses JJSX for building user interfaces and supports both server-side and client-side rendering.
error_desc: The page you requested does not exist, or it was moved to a different version.
error_hint: If you followed a link from these docs, the target page is probably missing from the current version directory.
getting_started_intro: Learn how to set up a Carats project and get a server-rendered application running.
requirements_content: Carats uses Bun for package management and for running the development server. Bun transpiles TSX on the fly, so there is no separate compile step while developing. Node.js 20+ also works for production builds, but Bun is the supported path.
quickstart_desc: The fastest way to start is the official project generator. It writes a complete, working Carats application with facets, culets, a shared layout, SASS design tokens and tests, so every feature described in these docs is already wired up and can be read as working code.
quickstart_run: Install dependencies and start the dev server
quickstart_clone_desc: The generator is the recommended path, but the same project is published as a template and can be cloned directly.
gs_create_generator_note: `bun create carats` resolves the published `create-carats` package and runs its `create-carats` binary, which writes a complete Carats project into the directory you name. Pass no directory to scaffold into the current one.
gs_dev_server_note: The server listens on `http://localhost:5173`. The generated project ships with a dashboard, a market, a portfolio, a trade page, a shared layout, a not-found page and an error page, so every feature described in these docs is already wired up and can be read as working code.
gs_express5_note: `@carats/express` requires Express 5, so the major version is not optional.
gs_typeroots_note: `typeRoots` does double duty. It points at `src/dto` so the global DTO interfaces are picked up as declaration files, and it keeps `./node_modules` on the search path so `types: ["jjsx"]` resolves, since `jjsx` does not live under `@types`.
gs_app_entry_note: The main application file must live at `src/app.ts`.
manual_setup_desc: If you prefer to start from an empty project, create the folder structure below and install the dependencies yourself.
folder_structure_desc: Create the following folders and files. The locations are fixed because the framework resolves them by convention.
install_deps_desc: Carats is split into small packages. The runtime dependencies below are the ones used by a full-stack application; the dev dependencies are needed for JJSX transpilation, SASS and type checking.
tsconfig_desc: Carats requires a tsconfig.json at the root of the project. The types, jsx, jsxFactory and jsxFragmentFactory options are what teach TypeScript about JJSX, and typeRoots is what makes the global DTO interfaces in src/dto resolvable.
vite_client_desc: The client build runs in middleware mode because the Express server owns the HTTP listener. appType: 'custom' disables Vite's own HTML fallback, since Carats renders the HTML template itself.
package_scripts_desc: These scripts are the supported entry points for developing, building and previewing a Carats application.
run_desc: bun run dev starts the app with the Bun inspector on port 6499. bun run build bundles the server and the client, and bun run preview serves the production build. bun run build:static prerenders the app to static HTML.
structure_desc: A typical Carats project has the following structure:
desc_app_entry_point: Main application entry point. Mounts the Carats middleware on Express and starts the HTTP server.
desc_client_template: HTML template rendered by the server. Must contain the <!--app-head--> and <div id="app"><!--app-html--></div> placeholders.
desc_client_entrypoint: Client entrypoint. Mounts the facets on the browser and starts client-side rendering.
desc_route_definitions: Route definitions, shared by the client and the server entrypoint.
desc_vite_env: Vite client type reference. Lives at src/vite-env.d.ts, not inside src/client.
desc_base_sass: Global stylesheet holding the design tokens and base resets.
desc_pages: Page components. Each subfolder exports a default component from index.tsx and may import its own SASS file.
desc_server_entrypoint: Server entrypoint for SSR. Exports defineServerEntry(facets) and seats culets.
desc_server_functions: Culets, the server-side data functions used by burnished components.
desc_dto: Global TypeScript interfaces. Included through typeRoots so culet<User>(...) resolves without an import.
desc_public: Static assets served from the site root.
next_steps_desc: Read Core Concepts to understand how JJSX, facets, culets and server props fit together, then look at the Components and Server-Side Rendering pages.
core_concepts_intro: Understanding the core concepts of Carats will help you build applications more effectively.
jjsx_desc: JJSX enables a pure HTML & JavaScript experience similar to PHP. It allows you to write JavaScript code inside TSX files similar to React, but without React hooks or React DOM. Because components are plain functions that return HTML, the same component renders identically on the server and in the browser.
jjsx_compiles_note: JJSX compiles to a function call, so a component is an ordinary function that returns an HTML string. There is no virtual DOM to diff and no component instance to keep alive, which is why the same function is safe to run on the server and again in the browser.
facets_desc: Facets are the routing system in Carats. They are a single object that maps route patterns to page components, and the same object is used by both the client and the server, so a route can never drift between the two. Facets are defined in src/client/facets.cara.ts and may declare route parameters, suspense states and whether in-app routing is enabled.
facets_partial_note: defineFacets accepts a partial definition, so routes and suspense are both optional. The reference template only declares error and notFound; omit loading unless a page genuinely suspends.
facets_data_note: A facet is also the unit of data fetching. A route in `routes` is the route a culet must be registered under, and a page that is wrapped with `Burnish` receives the value that culet returned.
culets_desc: Culets are server-side functions that provide data to components. They are defined in src/server/culets and seated in the server entrypoint. Components that need server-side data are burnished, which makes the framework fetch from their culet automatically. A culet is matched to a page by its route string, so the route of the culet and the route of the facet must be identical.
culet_dynamic_params_note: With a dynamic route, the parameter is read from `req.params`:
seating_culets_desc: A culet defined in its own file is created with culet(route, handler) and then registered with seat(). seat returns the culet unchanged, so seating it is a pure registration step. Do not register the same culet a second time with another culet() call.
server_props_desc: Server props are the values a culet returns. The framework resolves them during server-side rendering, serializes them into the page, and passes them to the burnished component as its first argument. The component never fetches anything itself.
server_props_auto_text: Server props arrive as the first argument of a burnished component:
unburnished_page_note: A page that is not burnished simply receives no props, which is the normal case for a static page.
rendering_desc: Every page is rendered on the server first. The HTML template is filled in, the page component runs, and the resulting markup is sent to the browser together with the resolved server props. In the browser the same facets are mounted and the app takes over. A component function therefore runs in both places, which is why side effects must be deferred to afterMount or beforeMount.
rendering_twice_note: The practical consequence is that statements in a component body run twice in a normal page load: once on the server, once in the browser. Anything that touches `document`, reads `window` or performs a side effect has to be deferred to a hook, otherwise server-side rendering will throw.
client_runtime_desc: @carats/csr mounts the facets, intercepts internal link clicks when in-app routing is enabled, and exposes the serialized server props. window.carats.ssp.for holds the route the current server props belong to, and window.carats.ssp.data holds the props themselves. Prefer reading them through the framework rather than parsing the HTML, and use goTo for programmatic navigation.
goto_no_reload_note: `goTo` navigates the same way an intercepted link click does, so no document reload happens when in-app routing is enabled.
components_intro: Carats components are similar to React components but with some key differences in how they handle attributes and events.
component_structure_desc: Components are .tsx files that export a default function. They receive a single props object, may declare defaultProps, and render props.children where the children should appear. They can import any file Vite understands, which is how SASS is attached to a component.
sass_side_effect_note: The SASS file is imported for its side effect, which is what attaches the stylesheet to the page. A component may import anything Vite understands: SASS, CSS, JSON or images.
component_props_desc: Props are passed to components as expected, and children are contained within the component tags. A burnished component receives its culet's return value as props instead.
component_default_props_desc: defaultProps fills in props that were not supplied. This is the usual way to make a page renderable during a test, where no server props are available.
component_head_desc: Components can provide dynamic head tags (title, meta) by assigning to this.head inside the component function. The tags are collected during server-side rendering and injected into the <!--app-head--> placeholder of the HTML template.
component_head_note: this only exists in a component declared with the function keyword. An arrow function has no own this, so it cannot assign this.head; use a function declaration, or drop the head tags and keep the component as an arrow function. A regular arrow component is typed as CaratsComponent when it is used directly in a route, and as CaratsComponentWithThis when the annotation is needed for a plain function expression.
carats_component_type_note: The `CaratsComponent` type must be imported; it is exported by `@carats/render`. The `this` parameter is only a type annotation and is erased at compile time.
component_attributes_desc: HTML attributes are preserved as-is and are treated as strings. Unlike React, you cannot pass a function to an event attribute such as onclick or onsubmit; use addEventListener inside an afterMount callback instead. This is the single most common difference when porting React code.
function_attribute_note: The function is not a valid HTML attribute value, so it ends up in the markup as garbage and nothing is ever called.
other_event_attributes_note: The same rule applies to `onsubmit`, `oninput`, `onchange` and every other event attribute. Give the element an `id` and look it up inside a hook callback.
burnish_desc: Burnished components automatically fetch data from their culet. Wrap your component with the Burnish function from @carats/render to enable this feature. The wrapper matches the component's route to a culet of the same route, so both must be registered under an identical route string.
burnish_recast: The framework caches the most recent server props for a route. Pass { recast: true } to refetch on every render instead of reusing the cached value.
burnished_props_note: A burnished component still accepts props like any other component, which is what makes it testable without a server.
client_entrypoint_desc: The entrypoint mounts the facets in the browser and then starts client-side rendering. clientRender() is required whenever in-app routing is enabled, and it should be called after mount.
global_stylesheet_note: The global stylesheet is imported here rather than in a page, because it holds the design tokens and the base resets that every page relies on.
vite_config_desc: The client Vite config builds from src/client and emits to dist/client with a manifest, which lets the server reference the hashed entry file.
server_side_intro: Carats provides automatic server-side rendering (SSR) through its @carats/ssr package.
server_entrypoint_desc: The server entrypoint is defined in src/server/entrypoint.ts using defineServerEntry from @carats/ssr. It binds the shared facets, registers culets, and exposes the render and getServerProps functions used by the server plugin.
entry_drives_note: The object returned by `defineServerEntry` is what the server plugin drives:
entry_render_item: `render(req)` resolves the facet for the requested URL, runs the page component and returns the rendered `html` together with the collected `head` tags.
entry_props_item: `getServerProps(req)` resolves the culet for the requested URL and returns its value, or `undefined` when the route has no culet.
entry_facets_item: `facets` is the shared facets object, and `culets` is the registry built by `culet` and `seat`.
entry_default_export_note: This is why the default export must be the entry itself: the Express plugin calls these functions for every request.
culets_server_desc: Culets are defined using the culet function from @carats/ssr. Define one only when a route actually needs a server-side prop, and only when the data can be retrieved by a single GET request. The handler receives the request, including the route parameters, cookies, headers, query and method.
generic_param_note: The generic parameter is optional but worth keeping: it is what makes the return value match the props of the page that consumes it.
culet_seat_desc: A culet created in its own file must be registered with the seat function in the server entrypoint. Seating does not wrap or re-create the culet; it returns the same function so it can be used inline.
inline_culet_note: A culet declared inline in the entrypoint registers itself, so it needs no `seat` call. A culet imported from `src/server/culets` was created by `culet()` in its own module and must be seated once. Do not wrap a seated culet in another `culet()` call, because that would register the same handler under a second route.
express_integration_desc: Carats is integrated with Express through @carats/express. The exported carats function returns a Router that renders pages, resolves server props and serves the built client assets, so it is mounted with app.use. This package requires Express 5.
middleware_order_note: Order the middleware so that `carats()` runs after the routes and static handlers it should not swallow. The plugin returns an Express `Router`, which is why it is mounted with `app.use` rather than registered as a route.
server_vite_config_desc: The server bundle is built from src/server/entrypoint.ts into dist/server. publicDir is disabled because static assets belong to the client build.
route_match_warning: Note that the facet route and the culet route are identical strings, including the `:symbol` parameter. A mismatch is the most common reason a burnished page renders without data.
hooks_intro: Carats gives you state and a client-side lifecycle through the @carats/hooks package.
use_hook_desc: The use function provides state management. Unlike React hooks it is not reactive: setting a value does not re-render anything, so nothing on the page updates by itself. The other half of the pair is subscribe, which is how a change becomes visible. Read the value while rendering, write the DOM from a subscriber, and change the value from anywhere.
use_manual_dom_note: Because there is no re-render, read the value while rendering and write the DOM from a subscriber:
use_interface: The use function returns a State object with get, set and subscribe methods. set accepts either a new value or a factory that receives the current one.
set_returns_note: set returns the new value, so you can use the result straight away when you need the updated number immediately.
use_outside_component_note: `use` is also callable outside a component, which is the idiomatic way to share a single piece of state between pages.
subscribe_note: subscribe returns an unsubscribe function. Call it from the clear callback of an afterMount or beforeMount hook, otherwise the subscriber stays registered after the page is replaced.
subscribe_owns_dom_note: Keep the two concerns apart. A handler changes state and a subscriber writes the DOM. A handler that also writes the DOM gives the element two sources of truth, and the moment one of them is missed the page disagrees with itself.
aftermount_desc: The afterMount callback runs only on the client side, after the load event has been dispatched. Use it to reach DOM elements that the same component created, such as a counter label or a button. It may return a clear callback, which runs before the next hydration pass.
handler_identity_note: Keep a reference to the exact handler you registered. Passing a fresh arrow function to `removeEventListener` creates a new function identity, so the listener is never actually removed.
beforemount_desc: The beforeMount callback runs immediately on the client side, without waiting for the load event. Use it for work that does not need the markup of the component itself, such as timers, key listeners or subscriptions. Like afterMount, it may return a clear callback.
choosing_mount_hook_note: Reach for afterMount when the work depends on the markup this component produced, because it runs after the load event and the document is then guaranteed to be complete. Reach for beforeMount when it does not, such as a timer or a key listener, so that the work starts sooner.
clear_hydrations_desc: Clears all registered hydration callbacks by running their clear callbacks. This is mainly useful in tests and when tearing down an app manually.
hooks_no_react_note: There is no useEffect and no dependency array in Carats. A hook body runs on the server and on the client, so anything that touches the DOM or the network has to live inside a hook callback.
styling_intro: Carats uses scoped SASS for styling, promoting semantic HTML with minimal CSS classes.
base_sass_desc: The base.sass file in src/client contains global design tokens and style resets. All other SASS files import it with @use and as * so the tokens are available without a namespace prefix.
design_tokens_desc: Define colors, spacing, typography, breakpoints and other design tokens at the top level of base.sass. Do not nest them.
token_scope_note: A token defined inside a rule only exists inside that rule, so any other stylesheet that needs it has to redefine it. This is how a palette quietly drifts apart across a project.
semantic_html_desc: Prefer semantic HTML elements with minimal class usage. Let the component structure and the design tokens handle the styling, and nest selectors in SASS instead of adding utility classes to the markup.
best_practices_intro: Follow these best practices for maintainable styling:
best_practice1: Define tokens at the top level. Never nest design tokens inside mixins or functions.
best_practice2: Prefer semantic HTML. Let the structure define the styling instead of adding classes.
best_practice3: Import base.sass correctly. Always use @use 'relative/path/to/base.sass' as *.
best_practice4: Keep specificity low. Avoid deeply nested selectors.
best_practice5: Use variables for consistency. Never hardcode colors, spacing or sizes.
routing_intro: Routing in Carats is data, not a filesystem. Every route is declared in a single facets object that the client and the server share.
routes_desc: The routes map goes from a route pattern to a page component. The pattern is matched exactly, except for segments that start with a colon, which capture a parameter.
folder_name_convention_note: A page folder name is a convention, not a requirement. The folder keeps related files together, but the route a folder serves is whatever string it is mapped to, so `/market` can live in a folder called `browse` if that reads better.
dynamic_params_desc: A :name segment becomes a prop on the page component, and it is also available as params.name inside a culet for the same route. The name must match on both sides.
trade_btc_note: `/trade/btc` renders this page with `data.symbol` resolved from the culet registered for the same route, and the page renders a different `<title>` for every symbol. The framework does the matching in `getPageComponent`, which returns the component, the extracted `params` and the matched `route`.
route_matching_note: Route patterns are matched by @carats/url with matchRoute. There is no wildcard, no optional segment and no catch-all: an unmatched URL renders the notFound suspense component instead.
in_app_routing_desc: With inAppRouting enabled, the client intercepts clicks on internal anchors and swaps the page without a full page load. It also requires clientRender() in the client entrypoint. Turn it off when a page depends on a full document load, for example a page that must run a third-party script on every navigation.
mount_clientrender_note: Both lines are required when in-app routing is on. `mount` registers the facets in the browser, and `clientRender` starts intercepting navigation.
plain_links_note: Links need no framework component. A plain anchor is intercepted automatically, and a normal link is followed normally if the interception is disabled, which means pages stay crawlable and work without JavaScript.
goto_desc: goTo from @carats/csr navigates the same way an intercepted link click does. It is the right way to submit a search box or any other form that should not reload the document.
query_params_note: Build the query string with the standard `URLSearchParams`, which handles the encoding for you. To read the parameters of the current route from a component, ask a culet for them: a culet receives the matched parameters in `req.params`, and the page receives whatever the culet returned.
routing_suspense_desc: The suspense map supplies the components used when a route cannot produce a page: notFound for an unmatched URL and error for a component or culet that threw. Both are optional, and error receives the thrown Error as its only argument.
wrap_in_layout_note: Wrap both in the shared layout. A failing page that renders without the site chrome is much harder to diagnose than one that keeps the header and navigation.
data_fetching_intro: Server props are the only data channel Carats provides. A culet fetches on the server, and a burnished component receives the result.
culet_lifecycle_desc: The server resolves the culet for the requested route before the page component runs, so the component always renders with complete data and there is no loading state to handle. When a culet throws, the error is passed to the error suspense component.
thrown_error_note: A thrown error, whether from the culet or from the component, reaches the `error` suspense component as an `Error`. An unmatched URL reaches `notFound` instead.
culet_args_desc: A culet handler receives everything the request carried: params for the route parameters, plus url, query, headers, cookies and method. There is no data property, because culets are only ever reached by a GET.
per_visitor_note: Because `cookies` and `headers` are available, a culet can personalise a page per visitor without any extra plumbing. The response is still cached per route, so do not put per-visident data in a culet that is not marked `recast` on the consuming component.
async_desc: A culet can be async, and awaiting inside it is the normal way to talk to a database or a remote API. Returning a promise is enough; there is no need to await it at the call site.
caching_desc: The framework keeps the most recent server props for a route and reuses them, so a burnished component does not refetch on every render. When a page must always show fresh data, opt out per component with the recast option.
recast_desc: Wrap the component with { recast: true } to bypass the cache on every render. It applies to that component only, which makes it a good fit for pages such as a live dashboard rather than a whole-site default.
no_implicit_match_note: There is no implicit matching by file name or by component name. A typo in the route string fails silently: the page renders, the props are `undefined`, and the error surfaces as a crash inside the component. Registering the culet route as a named constant and importing it into both places removes the failure mode.
recast_on_component_note: `recast` belongs on the component, not on the culet, so a single live page does not force every consumer of that route to refetch.
ssp_global_desc: The serialized props are exposed on window.carats.ssp. ssp.for is the route they belong to and ssp.data is the value. This is what lets a non-burnished component, or plain code in an afterMount callback, read data that the server already fetched, instead of issuing a second request.
ssp_typed_note: The client global is typed, so `window.carats` needs no cast. `ssp.for` is the route the payload belongs to, which lets a shared component verify that the data it is about to read was resolved for the page it is rendered on, and skip it when it was not.
culet_matching_desc: A culet is bound to its page purely by route string. The route of the culet and the route of the facet must be character-for-character identical, including parameter names, otherwise the component renders without data. A route with no culet simply renders with no props, which is the normal case for static pages.
testing_intro: Components and culets are plain functions, so both can be tested directly. No DOM environment and no rendering library is required.
testing_desc: The test script runs Vitest with V8 coverage. Exclude the entrypoints, the facets file and the DTO folder from coverage, since they are wiring rather than logic.
testing_component_desc: Call init once from jjsx to install the transpiler, then call transpile with a JSX element to get the HTML string. Asserting on substrings of that string is usually enough and keeps the test free of a DOM.
testing_burnish_desc: A burnished component accepts its server props as ordinary props, so the same element renders with mock data in a test exactly as it would on the server.
init_transpiler_note: `init()` installs the JJSX transpiler and must run before the first `transpile` call. Because the result is a plain HTML string, there is no DOM to set up and no rendering library to configure.
testing_culet_desc: A culet is a function from a request to a value. Pass a plain object with params and call it. There is no server to start, which is the main reason culets are cheap to test.
fetch_mock_note: `@fetch-mock/vitest` is available for a culet that calls a remote API, which keeps the test offline and deterministic.
no_document_note: A component that reads `window` or `document` directly in its body cannot be transpiled in a test, because the test environment has no document. That is a useful signal rather than an obstacle: it means the side effect belongs in an `afterMount` or `beforeMount` callback, where the framework already keeps it out of the server render.
static_generation_intro: The @carats/ssg package prerenders a Carats application to static HTML, which is useful for sites that do not need a live server.
static_generation_desc: Add the static build script to package.json. It runs the carats-ssg binary with NODE_ENV=production, so the same build pipeline produces the static output.
ssg_binary_note: The `carats-ssg` binary comes from the `@carats/ssg` package, which is why it is a runtime dependency rather than a dev dependency: the prerendered output is a deployment artifact.
static_generation_note1: Content that is the same for every visitor, such as marketing pages and documentation.
static_generation_note2: Deployments that only need a CDN or a file host.
static_generation_note3: Sites that still need per-request data should use the Express integration instead, because a culet may depend on the request.
static_generation_cli_note: The carats-ssg binary ships no TypeScript declarations of its own; treat it as a command-line tool and keep the framework types in @carats/ssr.
ssg_per_request_note: A culet may read cookies, headers or the query string. Any route backed by such a culet cannot be meaningfully prerendered, because the output would be frozen with one visitor's data. Keep those routes on the SSR build, or mark the consuming component with `{ recast: true }` and accept that the static output holds placeholder data.
api_reference_intro: Every @carats/* package is small and fully typed. The declarations below are the complete public surface.
define_facets_note: `defineFacets` takes a `PartialFacets` and returns a fully populated `Facets`, which is why every key of the input is optional. `Facets['suspense']` lists all three states, but the partial input allows declaring only the ones that matter.
head_note: `head` is a `JSX.Element`, not a string. Assign a fragment of tags to it, and the framework collects the fragment during rendering.
get_page_component_note: `getPageComponent` is the function the server plugin is built on. It is exported because it is useful on its own: given a URL it resolves a component plus its parameters, which is enough to work out what a request would render.
is_handled_note: The `_isHandled` flag on `HTMLAnchorElement` is how the runtime marks a link it has already taken over. Once a link has been handled, navigation happens in the client instead of the browser. Do not set it yourself.
culet_args_note: `CuletArgs` is `CaratsRequest` without `data`, plus `params`. The absence of `data` is deliberate: a culet is only ever reached by a GET, so there is no request body to read.
ssg_no_exports_note: `@carats/ssg` ships a command-line tool and no runtime exports, so it has no importable surface. It is referenced by the `build:static` script and nowhere in application code.
conventions_intro: Carats resolves a handful of paths and filenames by convention. Deviating from them works until it does not, so it is worth keeping to them.
conv_pages_desc: Each route lives in its own folder under src/client/pages, and the folder exports a default component from index.tsx next to a stylesheet of the same name. Folders that start with an underscore are not routes; they are shared building blocks referenced by the routes that need them.
underscore_folders_note: The leading underscore is what marks a folder as a building block rather than a page. It keeps shared components out of the way in the file tree and signals that they are not meant to be routed to.
conv_layout_desc: There is no file-convention layout like Next.js. A _layout component is imported by the pages that need it, which makes the composition explicit and lets a page opt out. The reference template wraps every page in the same layout to share the header, the footer and the mobile menu.
layout_children_note: The layout renders `props.children` where the page content belongs, which is the only composition mechanism. There is no nested-route tree and no automatic wrapping, so the dependency is visible in the import.
conv_error_desc: The error and notFound suspense components are ordinary components. The error one receives the thrown Error, so it can read message and stack; the notFound one receives nothing. Both are worth wrapping in the shared layout so a failure still renders the site chrome.
conv_dto_desc: Interfaces placed in src/dto are global, because typeRoots points at that folder. That is what lets a culet be written as culet<User> with no import in both the server entrypoint and the page component. Keep these files free of imports and runtime code; they are declarations only.
dto_no_export_note: The interface has no `export`, which is what makes it global. With `typeRoots` pointing at `src/dto`, `culet<User>` and `Burnish<User>` resolve in every file without an import, and a rename in one place is picked up everywhere.
conv_sass_desc: A page or component imports its own SASS file, and that file imports base.sass with @use ... as *. The extension is optional in the path. Keep global resets and tokens in base.sass and nothing else there.
sass_use_path_note: The extension in the `@use` path is optional, and the path is relative to the stylesheet rather than to the component. `base.sass` is the only file that defines tokens; every other file consumes them.
conv_naming_desc: Route folders are named after the route segment, and the dynamic parameter name must be identical in the facet and in the culet. Culet files are named after the action they perform and default export the culet, which is then seated in the server entrypoint.
react_migration_intro: Carats is deliberately close to React, so most component code ports directly. The differences below are the ones that actually break a port.
rm_row_runtime_react: React, React DOM and a virtual DOM
rm_row_runtime_carats: JJSX only; components are functions returning HTML
rm_row_state_carats: use stores a value; the DOM is updated manually
rm_row_effect_carats: afterMount (after load) or beforeMount (immediate), no deps
rm_row_routing_react: A file-system router with layouts and nested routes
rm_row_routing_carats: A defineFacets map, composed by importing a layout
rm_row_data_carats: A culet per route plus a Burnish wrapper
rm_row_head_react: next/head or the framework metadata export
rm_row_meta_carats: defaultProps on the component; no context or memo
rm_row_styling_carats: Scoped SASS importing shared design tokens
rm_events_intro: The event model is the change that breaks a port most often, so it is worth being precise about it.
rm_state_desc: `useState` becomes `use`, and every render that React would have handled becomes an explicit DOM write. State that was local to a component is unchanged in spirit: call `use` at the top level of the component, read it with `get`, and write with `set`.
rm_routing_desc: The file-system router collapses into a single object. Every route becomes an entry in `defineFacets`, and nested layouts become an explicit import. Because the facets object is shared, a route that is missing from it is missing from both the client and the server, which removes a whole class of bug.
rm_data_desc: `getServerSideProps` becomes a culet, and the page becomes burnished. The function signature is the same shape: the request in, the data out.
rm_head_desc: A metadata export becomes `this.head`, and the component has to be a `function` declaration for `this` to exist. A component that is already an arrow function can stay one, at the cost of not contributing head tags.
rm_styling_desc: CSS-in-JS has no equivalent. Each component imports a SASS file, that file imports `base.sass` for the design tokens, and the tokens live at the top level of that one global stylesheet.
rm_step1: Delete react, react-dom and every React-only dependency.
rm_step2: Replace event attributes with addEventListener inside an afterMount or beforeMount callback.
rm_step3: Convert every file-based route into an entry in the facets map, and import a shared layout explicitly.
rm_step4: Move getServerSideProps bodies into culets, and wrap the page with Burnish.
rm_step5: Move useState to use, and add the manual DOM update that the re-render used to do.
rm_step6: Move the head export to this.head on a function component.
rm_step7: Replace CSS-in-JS with SASS files imported by each component.
